subject: Displacement risk: benchmark request & capacity uplift proposal
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cartlane.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cartlane.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark request — proof for alternative vendor evaluation

Ava,

We’re running a competitive evaluation right now and I need a quick proof-point from Redwood to keep you in the running. Procurement + our AI infra team plan to pilot a replacement vendor (ZephyrAI) later this month unless we see better latency/cost for our peak pattern.

Ask: can Redwood run a small, customer-specific benchmark that mirrors our typical workload (attached)? Key outputs we need: P50/P95/P99 latencies at 2M tokens/month baseline, 1k RPS burst profile, memory/kv-cache behavior for 4k context, and a firm cost estimate for a Dedicated uplift (committed capacity).

We also want to understand contract levers: if Cartlane commits to a 12-month uplift, what incremental discount and SLA improvements can you offer?

Attached: RFP-snapshot-2027.pdf (short requirements)

This is time-sensitive — procurement asked for results by next Thursday.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of ML Ops
Cartlane

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cartlane.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark request — proof for alternative vendor evaluation

Elena — thank you for the clear ask and the RFP snapshot. We can run the benchmark and produce the latency percentiles and an apples-to-apples cost model.

Next steps I propose:
- We run a 48-hour synthetic run against a mirrored model stack using your sample traces.
- Provide P50/P95/P99 for token generation and end-to-end tail latencies with and without KV cache warm.
- Deliver a Dedicated uplift pricing sheet with two options: 6-month trial (no commitment) and 12-month committed tier with discounted unit cost and a 99.9% tail SLA.

Can you send the sample traces and a list of peak hours (your timezone)? If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min sync today to align scope — Jonas (cc) will own the technical run.

I’ll attach a draft SOW and the benchmark plan after we confirm traces.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOW-draft-blank.docx]

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cartlane.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@cartlane.com>, procurement@cartlane.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark request — proof for alternative vendor evaluation

Thanks Ava. Attached are: Cartlane_sample_traces.jsonl and a short note on peak windows (PST business hours, high traffic Tue/Thu 11:00–13:00).

FYI — ZephyrAI is offering a pilot with aggressive pricing and a short-term capacity guarantee. We’re not committed to moving, but they’ve asked for a test window this month. If Redwood can produce the benchmark + a competitive committed uplift offer, we’ll prioritize your results in our procurement review.

Please keep the run reproducible and include exact model versions and quantization settings.

Elena

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Cartlane save plan — proposed options

Team — quick note while the traces are running. Summary of the situation: Cartlane is evaluating ZephyrAI; procurement pressured for decision next week. They want a benchmark + committed uplift pricing.

Proposed options (we should pick a primary + fallback):
1) 12-month committed uplift: 15% off hosted token rates, Dedicated pool with reserved throughput, 99.9% p99 SLA, rolling canary. Offer: 60% commitment on expected baseline (reduces unit price).
2) 6-month trial (no commitment): benchmark + proof window, 10% discount if they convert within 30 days, no change to SLA.
3) Technical concession: allow a one-month rollback clause and an automatic fallback to a smaller uncommitted pool in case early regressions.

Risks: finance wants to avoid deep discounts without capacity commitment. Product/infra needs to confirm we can meet 1k RPS spikes with the proposed Dedicated config without impacting other tenants.

Action items: Jonas to confirm infra feasibility and provide estimated infra cost. Karthik to prep legal language for rollback and trial clause. I’ll draft the customer-facing benchmark report and the SOW.

- Ava

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cartlane.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Cartlane — benchmark results and capacity uplift proposal (attached)

Elena, Ravi — thanks for the traces and patience. Attached are the benchmark artifacts: Cartlane_benchmark_results_v2.pdf (latency tables, tail behavior, test config) and a draft SOW (SOW-draft-CapacityUplift.xlsx) that lays out two commercial options. Highlights: 

- Latency: P50=78ms, P95=210ms, P99=380ms on our Dedicated baseline with warmed KV cache (4k context). End-to-end tail latency during 1k RPS synthetic bursts matched the required profile; we observed no significant degradation for colocated workloads.
- Cost: Two proposals — 6-month proof (no commit) at list-hosted rates with a 10% conversion credit; 12-month committed uplift with a 15% unit discount and a capacity reservation that reduces your operational token cost by ~28% vs. unreserved usage.
- SLA: For the committed 12-month option we will include a 99.9% p99 SLA, dedicated capacity pools, and a rollback clause (30 days) if peak performance regressions occur.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Executive procurement + CS sync to review SOW and SLA items (30–45 minutes).
2) If acceptable, we’ll send a DocuSign with the committed uplift and SOW.

Attachments: Cartlane_benchmark_results_v2.pdf, SOW-draft-CapacityUplift.xlsx

Would you be available Wednesday for a 30-min call?

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
[attachment: Cartlane_benchmark_results_v2.pdf]
[attachment: SOW-draft-CapacityUplift.xlsx]

From: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@cartlane.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cartlane.com>, procurement@cartlane.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 17:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cartlane — benchmark results and capacity uplift proposal (attached)

Ava / Jonas — thanks for the thorough report. Procurement reviewed the numbers and the committed uplift looks reasonable compared to our internal forecasts. We’re prepared to move forward on the 12-month committed option subject to two clarifications before DocuSign:

1) Rollback protection: we need the 30-day rollback clause explicitly spelled into the SOW with objective performance gates (P95/P99 thresholds).
2) Trial sprint: we want a 14-day production pilot window after go-live to validate the SLA during real traffic.

If you can include these items in the final SOW we’ll sign and send the payment/PO within 5 business days. Please send the DocuSign link once updated.

Ravi Shah
Senior Procurement Manager
Cartlane

[procurement@cartlane.com]
